confirmed.fact: The management auth RPC set contains register, approve and reject, but no pending-auth metadata read RPC. Approve and reject accept only auth_id and return empty messages.
Headscale internally stores an immutable SSH source/destination node pair on the pending auth request. It is not exposed by the management API, and the binding does not store the login username.
The destination-authenticated Noise SSH action handler logs local_user but does not pass it into the cached auth binding. It returns or waits for SSH decisions, not a UI metadata document.

Without OIDC, GET /auth/{auth_id} only renders a CLI approval instruction. With OIDC, this route starts an authentication flow whose callback can finish the auth decision; it is not a side-effect-free metadata API.

The product already discloses the missing trusted source/target/login-user summary and requires a trusted-channel check. Current SSH decisions send only the Auth ID and do not infer metadata from the selected registration user.

requiredExternalContract.description: An authenticated, side-effect-free, expiry-aware read of a server-bound pending SSH request, including trusted source node/identity, destination node and the originally bound login username. The username must first be retained in trusted server-side request metadata.
requiredExternalContract.approvalRequired: Explicit authorization to change the external Headscale service contract or repository; not authorized in this task.

authorizationBoundary: No source/target/user summary inferred from opaque Auth IDs, caller-supplied URL parameters or the selected registration owner.
No synthetic backend endpoint, direct database access, Noise impersonation or bypass of approval.
No product source, shared harness, external repository, deployment or production data changed.
verificationLimit: This is a pinned-source contract audit and archived UI evidence check, not a new browser execution. The separate G18 probe tests normal decision APIs on fresh real SSH requests and must not be reported as a UI rerun.
